title: Mya Has the Glass
hook: Mya owns the glass. The log is still open.
scene: The Ledger's cab is a high seat and a thermos that has been empty since yesterday. Mya is a brown mackerel loaf on the dash, dark stripe, green eyes, one paw in the west-coast glass. The clipboard is clipped to the doghouse. Amber vest, taped shoulder. Ali is still in the jump seat from the ride-along. Your hands are on the wheel now. The arterial is already moving.
debrief: This is Deac's cab: west-coast mirrors, thermos, log, cat on the dash. If you cannot see past Mya, move her. The glass is the job.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: Establish the Ledger cab: high seat, west-coast mirrors, Mya blocking glass, clipboard as the log.

title: The Right Is Through
hook: Two southbound lanes. A sedan is camping left.
scene: Central Avenue, two lanes south, rain on a Kent morning. A primer sedan is doing twenty-eight in the left. Your lane is the right. The left looks empty ahead of him. The thermos ticks once in the cup. Schedule wants the hole. The Ledger is long and the next light is already a rumor.
decision: The left lane is open ahead of a slow sedan. Where do you put this bus?

options.text: Move left now and sit in the empty — through traffic can use either
options.result: You take the left and become the new slow. A pickup that was using that lane as a pass has to stand on it. Horn. The sedan never moved. You spent his margin to sit pretty.

options.text: Hold the right. Pass only if he stays slow and the left is clear
options.result: You stay right. He stays twenty-eight. When the left is empty and you need him, you take it, clear him, and come back. The pickup behind never has to lift. Through traffic stayed through.

options.text: Straddle both — the Ledger is wide enough that the sedan will yield
options.result: You occupy the dashed line. He brakes. The pickup goes for the shoulder. You own two lanes and nobody can pass you, including you.

options.text: Drop to twenty and wait for him to notice and move over
options.result: You become a rolling roadblock in the right. He never looks. The stack behind you grows. You taught the arterial that the Ledger is the problem.

debrief: When several lanes go the same way, through traffic keeps right except to pass. Sitting in the left because it looks empty makes you the thing other people have to pass.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Keep right except to pass on a multi-lane road; the left is for passing, not cruising.

title: Rooms You Cannot See
hook: Fog eats the right glass. The sweep is the job.
scene: Fog eats the right glass on a mill-and-fill at midday. Cones pinch the right lane shut. You need left. The Ledger has rooms a Beetle never had: a whole van-length of nothing in the west-coast, and a convex that lies if you stare at it once. The thermos is still empty. Your eyes want the hole, not the sweep.
decision: You need the left lane. What do you look at, and in what order?

options.text: Glance the left glass once and go — you already know the right is cones
options.result: You take the left on one look. A motorcycle you never owned is in the room the convex would have shown. He stands on it. You stand on it. The cones get a new story.

options.text: Watch the hole until it is yours, then check the glass as you commit
options.result: The hole closes while your eyes are in it. You drift. A cone kisses the skirting. The sweep you skipped was the only thing that would have told you the hole was a rumor.

options.text: Left glass, right glass, convex, over the shoulder, then the hole
options.result: You run the rooms. The convex has a motorcycle in it that the flat glass missed. You wait one more gap. When you take it, he is already past. The cones stay cones.

options.text: Trust the convex alone — it sees more than the flats
options.result: The convex shrinks a pickup into a toy. You take the hole on a toy. He is a wall. You put the Ledger's shoulder in his.

debrief: The Ledger has rooms you cannot see unless you sweep them. Glass, convex, shoulder, then the hole. One look is a guess. Named in Skill nine.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Mirror sweep plus over-the-shoulder before a lane change; convex glass lies if it is the only look.

title: The Right-Side Room
hook: A white panel sits in the convex. You are already signaling.
scene: Clear cold afternoon on West Valley. You signaled left a breath ago. In the right convex, a white panel van is parked in the room the Ledger cannot see from the seat — close, same heading, no lamps. If you drift right to make the left feel bigger, you write him into the skirting. The blinker is already talking.
decision: The convex has a van in the right-side room and you are mid-change. What do you do?

options.text: Cancel, hold the lane, let him show or fall back, then take a clean hole
options.result: You kill the blinker and hold. He appears in the flat glass a second later, then drops. The next hole is empty. You take it without writing him into the steel.

options.text: Finish the left — he is on the right, so the left is yours
options.result: You commit left. The van was using you as a windbreak and comes with you. Steel on steel. He never had lamps. You never had the room.

options.text: Drift right first to square up, then take the left
options.result: You drift into the room to get a better angle. The convex was already telling you the room was occupied. The panel takes the skirting. That was the timeout.

options.text: Tap the horn so he knows to get out of the convex
options.result: The horn on an arterial. He flinches into you. You both stop in a live lane. Everything behind has to lift.

debrief: If you cannot see him in the glass, assume he is in the room. Cancel, hold, then take a hole you have swept. The convex is a check, not a suggestion.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Recheck the blind zone during a lane change; do not drift into a vehicle the convex already showed.

title: A Hundred Feet of Amber
hook: Amber letters crawl. The column has not seen you yet.
scene: Wind at dusk on 167, a three-vehicle stack you did not ask for. You need the left in a hundred feet. Radios are trash. The Ledger talks with amber — your sign, your stalk. If you wink the stalk at the last second, the box behind you will eat your rear doors.
decision: You need the left in a hundred feet. How do you tell the column?

options.text: Move first, then signal — they will see the bus and understand
options.result: You start the change. The box behind had no sentence. He stands on it. You stand on it. The sign stays dark. You spent his brakes to keep your schedule.

options.text: Flash the highs twice — faster than a blinker and they cannot miss it
options.result: The flash hits his glass and comes back. He thinks you are warning him of something ahead. He slows in your hole. You still have not said left.

options.text: Leave the sign dark and use the stalk at the last skip-dash
options.result: The stalk talks for ten feet. He is already in your door. Late is the same as silent on a bus this long.

options.text: Sign left, stalk on, hold a hundred feet, then take a swept hole
options.result: Amber crawls LEFT. The stalk agrees. You hold the lane until the box lifts. The hole you take is one he already gave you. That is a sentence.

debrief: Signal a hundred feet before you move. The destination sign is the same sentence for a column that cannot hear you. Late amber is a surprise, not a signal.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Signal at least 100 feet before a lane change; give the column time to answer.

title: If You Cannot Count It
hook: The hole looks like a hole. Count it anyway.
scene: Heavy rain at night on Meeker. You need the left. A gap opens between a pickup and a dark SUV. It looks like a Ledger-shaped hole. Your foot agrees. The ride-along is still in your hands: if you cannot count it, it is not a hole. The thermos does not argue. The schedule does.
decision: A gap just opened in the left. Do you take it?

options.text: Hold until you can count a full Ledger plus a breath, then take it
options.result: You wait. The SUV closes what looked like a hole. The next gap is longer. You count it, take it, and nobody has to lift. Late on the log. Alive in the lane.

options.text: Take it now — rain makes people generous and the pickup already lifted
options.result: You put the nose in. The SUV did not lift. You make him. Horn, spray, the Ledger's shoulder in his. That was the late merge you already watched.

options.text: Nose in and force the zipper — they will make room for a bus
options.result: You write your length into a gap that was a car. He stands on it. You stand on it. Two lanes become one argument.

options.text: Match the pickup's speed in the right and wait for him to wave you in
options.result: He never waves. You sit beside him in the rain until the light. You did not count a hole. You waited for permission the arterial does not give.

debrief: Merge only into a gap you can count — your length, plus room so nobody has to swerve or stand on it. A hole you cannot count is a wish.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Accept only a merge gap large enough that other drivers need not swerve, slow, or stop.

title: Broken White, Solid White
hook: Broken white on the left. Solid white on the right.
scene: Snow at deep night on 84th. Two whites. The left skip-dash is broken — a legal change if the hole is real. The right is a solid white at the edge of a diamond lane you have not earned. The Ledger wants out of the stack. The paint is the sentence, not the want.
decision: You want out of this stack. Which paint do you cross?

options.text: Cross the solid white into the diamond — it is empty and faster
options.result: You take the diamond. The sign said two. You are one and a bus. A trooper remnant in a dark cap sits in the next ramp. You just wrote a restricted lane onto the log.

options.text: Straddle the broken white until someone makes a hole
options.result: You occupy the dash. Both lanes lose you. The stack behind has to guess which room you want. Nobody guesses right.

options.text: Wait for a hole and cross only the broken white. Leave the solid alone
options.result: You hold. A hole opens on the broken side. You take it, cancel, and leave the diamond to the people who paid for it. The paint stayed a sentence.

options.text: Use the solid as a shoulder to let the stack pass, then come back
options.result: The solid was not a shoulder. You put a bus on the rumble. Snow and a drain. The stack passes you as a wreck.

debrief: Broken white between same-direction lanes may be crossed to change lanes. Solid white marks an edge or a restricted lane — do not treat it as a passing lane or a shoulder.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Cross broken white to change lanes; do not cross solid white into a restricted or edge lane.

title: Hollis at Arterial Speed
hook: Hollis fills the glass. Your front gap is the fix.
scene: Ice on a Kent morning, 256th doing arterial speed. Hollis is in the lifted truck again, filling the interior glass, close enough that his plow is a suggestion. If you brake for the light you cannot see yet, he writes you into the doghouse. The six-second habit from the Grid still works. You just have to spend it ahead, not behind.
decision: Hollis is on your bumper at speed. What do you change?

options.text: Brake-check him once so he finds a legal following distance
options.result: You tap. He does not have ice tires. He has a lift and a wish. His plow kisses your rear doors. The arterial hears it.

options.text: Open your own front gap and hold speed so you can roll instead of stand on it
options.result: You lift a breath off the truck ahead. The next light goes yellow. You roll it out instead of planting. Hollis has to lift with you or eat you. He lifts. You never touched him.

options.text: Move left now and let him have this lane
options.result: You take a hole you did not sweep because he is loud. A sedan is in the left room. You make three problems out of one bumper.

options.text: Match him and close the front — if you are a box he cannot hit you as hard
options.result: You close the front. The light you could not see is red. You and Hollis and the truck ahead become one piece of ice.

debrief: When someone tailgates, increase YOUR following distance so you can avoid a panic stop. You cannot fix his bumper. You can refuse to be the middle of a chain.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: If tailgated, increase the gap ahead so you can brake gradually; do not brake-check.

title: The Panel Again
hook: Same white panel. Same room. He remembered you.
scene: Clear cold afternoon on West Valley, same paint, same sun angle. The white panel van is in the right-side room again, closer, lamps still off. Last time you drifted into him. This time he is already hugging the Ledger like a grudge. The blinker wants left. The convex is honest. He is not a surprise anymore. He is a debt.
decision: The van is in the right-side room and you still need left. What do you do with the debt?

options.text: Hold, let him declare, and take a hole you have swept twice
options.result: You hold. He finally shows a lamp and drops back. The hole you take is empty. He does not get a second kiss of steel. That is the apology.

options.text: Finish the left fast so he cannot stay in your room
options.result: You snatch the left. He comes with you again. Same steel, same afternoon. He was waiting for the same move.

options.text: Drift right and pin him to the curb so he cannot follow
options.result: You use the bus as a wall. He has nowhere. The curb takes his wheel. You collected the debt with his quarter panel.

options.text: Stop in the lane and wait until he goes around
options.result: You plant a bus on West Valley. He goes around into the left you wanted. Everyone behind you gets a new problem.

debrief: A miss in the right-side room comes back on the same street. Sweep, hold, then move. He does not owe you a hole because you already hit him once.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Revisit the blind-zone lane change: cancel and hold until the adjacent room is empty.

title: Old Ninety's Glass
hook: Old Ninety's trailer. If you cannot see his mirrors, he cannot.
scene: Overcast midday on 167. A rogue semi with no door marks and a dirty number that used to be ninety fills the rear glass, then the left. Old Ninety. You are beside a trailer that has rooms a Ledger understands. If you cannot see his west-coasts, you are nowhere. The schedule wants you past him. Nowhere wants you first.
decision: You are coming up on Old Ninety's left rear quarter. Where do you sit?

options.text: Hold beside the trailer — his length is a windbreak and the left is empty
options.result: You cruise the no-zone. He starts a right that needs your lane. You are the car in the statistic. He never had you in the glass.

options.text: Tuck under his tail — if you cannot see him he cannot hit you
options.result: You sit in the hole behind a loaded trailer. He cannot see you and he cannot stop for you. The next brake is yours.

options.text: Pass on the shoulder — the rumble is safer than his left
options.result: The shoulder is a drain and a sign post. You put a bus in the junk. He never knew you tried.

options.text: Drop back until both his mirrors show you, or commit the pass and clear
options.result: You fall back until two dirty west-coasts hold a Ledger. Then you pass once, all the way, and you do not linger. He keeps his rooms. You keep your steel.

debrief: If you cannot see a truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Do not live beside the trailer. Be in his glass, or be gone.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Stay out of a truck's blind zones; if you cannot see the driver's mirrors, you are invisible.

title: Do Not Live Beside
hook: The no-zones are drawn on the asphalt. Do not sit in them.
scene: Rain at dusk, still 167, the same trailer length painted in your head. Passing a truck is a trip, not a lane. If you linger at the drive axle you are in a room he uses to turn. The Ledger knows this from the other side. Tonight you are the car.
decision: You have started a pass on a trailer. When are you done?

options.text: When your nose is past his — that is enough to claim the lane
options.result: You recover early. Your rear doors are still at his drive axle. He starts the right he signaled a mile ago. You are the lingering car.

options.text: When you see his whole front in your glass and the bus is clear, then recover
options.result: You stay in the pass until the trailer is a trailer in the glass, not a wall at your shoulder. You recover once. He keeps his turn. You keep your doors.

options.text: Match his speed beside the cab so he sees you and can wave you past
options.result: You become a passenger on his left. He cannot wave a bus through a no-zone. He needs that space to live.

options.text: Cut in as soon as you see pavement in front of him — leave him a car length
options.result: You give a loaded trailer a car length at highway speed. He cannot stop. You just borrowed his stopping distance.

debrief: Do not linger beside a truck. Pass, then recover only when the whole front of his vehicle is in your mirror and you have left him stopping room.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Never linger beside a large vehicle; complete the pass and leave stopping room before merging back.

title: Twenty-Six, None Preventable
hook: Twenty-six years. The schedule is louder now.
scene: Fog on a downtown ramp at night, the Ledger idling in a legal pocket. Glasses on a cord. Clipboard on the thigh. Twenty-six years and he never wrote a preventable. The schedule used to be a promise to the people in the back. Now it is a number that wants the late merge you already refused. The thermos is still empty. That is not a boast. That is the cost of the number.
debrief: Deac's record is a habit, not a trophy. The schedule still matters. It does not get to spend someone else's margin. Two clean stops reset him. This idle is one.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: Deac beat: twenty-six years without a preventable; the schedule is not permission to take a late hole.

title: Arrow, Then Circle
hook: The arrow dies. The circle is still green.
scene: Clear cold dawn, high seat, a Kent arterial left-turn pocket. A green arrow has been feeding you. It dies. The circular green stays. Oncoming still has a path. The Ledger's nose is already in the intersection because you trusted the arrow. Permissive is not protected. The yellow line you want is still across a live lane.
decision: The arrow is gone and the circle is green. Do you finish the left?

options.text: Go now — you were in the intersection on the arrow, so you own it
options.result: You take the permissive as if it were still protected. Oncoming is a pair of lamps you did not yield to. You make them lift. The pocket was not a promise.

options.text: Sit in the pocket until another arrow — circular green is a trap
options.result: You become a bus in a pocket through two cycles. The stack behind you starts using the through lanes. You taught the light that Deac does not know the difference.

options.text: Yield to oncoming, then take the closest lane right of their yellow when it is clear
options.result: You wait. Oncoming clears. You steer to the first lane right of their yellow, not the far one. The arrow was a gift. The circle is a yield.

options.text: Swing wide into the far lane so you are out of oncoming's way faster
options.result: You exit into the far lane. A through car already owns it. You traded a yield for a sideswipe.

debrief: A green arrow is protected. A circular green is permissive — yield to oncoming, then finish in the closest lane to the right of the yellow. The arrow dying is the lesson, not a dare.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part two
source.teaching_target: Protected left on a green arrow; permissive circular green requires a yield, then the nearest lane right of the yellow.

title: The Pocket Is Not a Lane
hook: The pocket is for turns. The stack wants a pass.
scene: Wind on a Kent morning. A two-way left-turn lane down the middle, arrows both ways, the same idea as the Grid's dead-van pocket except this one is legal if you are actually turning. A primer sedan is using it as a travel lane to beat the light. Your left is coming up in two blocks. The pocket will take you. It will not take you for a mile.
decision: The two-way pocket is empty for a long stretch. How do you use it?

options.text: Enter only when you are ready to turn, and do not travel farther than you need
options.result: You wait until the turn is real. You take the pocket for a short bite, yield to the other direction, and finish. The sedan is still touring it like a lane when oncoming wants it.

options.text: Use it as a passing lane — that is what the dashes are for
options.result: You pass in a lane that belongs to both directions. Oncoming enters it to turn. Two noses, one paint. The dashes were not a pass.

options.text: Ride it for the next mile so you are already in position at every left
options.result: You travel the center. Three driveways and a car coming the other way all have a claim. Three hundred feet was the limit. You spent it like a highway.

options.text: Straddle the yellow and the pocket so nobody can surprise you
options.result: You occupy two rooms. Through traffic has to guess. The pocket is no longer a pocket. It is a problem with your name on it.

debrief: A two-way left-turn lane is for turning, not traveling or passing. Enter it to turn, watch the other direction, and do not tour it.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part two
source.teaching_target: Use a two-way left-turn lane only to turn; do not travel or pass in it.

title: The Hood Line Walks
hook: The hood line walks toward the rumble. Your eyes were gone.
scene: Overcast afternoon, a long straight on 167, nothing to do with your hands but hold. The thermos is empty. The hood line has walked an inch toward the rumble and you did not tell it to. That is the Drift with a lowercase d until you name it. A clean stop would reset it. There is no legal shoulder that is not a story. The timeout is the walk.
decision: The hood line is walking and you felt the skip. What do you do?

options.text: Shake it off and hold speed — the straight will end and you will be fine
options.result: You argue with a nervous system. The walk becomes a tire on the rumble. The stack behind you gets a new shape of bus.

options.text: Crack a window and talk — conversation is as good as a stop
options.result: You talk to an empty jump seat. The walk continues. Conversation is not sleep. The rumble finds you anyway.

options.text: Speed up so the air keeps you honest
options.result: You add speed to a microsleep. The Drift does not care about your schedule. It cares that you are still moving.

options.text: Signal, find a legal pad, key off, twenty minutes. The log can wait.
options.result: You take the next ramp pad, hazards, key off. Twenty minutes that are not driving. The hood line is a hood line when you start again. Two clean stops reset him. This is one.

debrief: Lane drift, heavy eyes, missing a stretch of road — pull off and rest. Fatigue is impairment. The schedule does not get a vote.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: Treat lane drift and a missing stretch of road as fatigue; stop and rest rather than push through.

title: The Convex Lies Down
hook: The convex hangs. The right-side room is gone.
scene: Heavy rain at dusk in a mill-and-fill. A cone you did not own kissed the right west-coast arm. The convex now looks at the sky. Mya is a loaf on the dash, useless for this. The Ledger just lost a room. You can keep rolling on a guess or you can make the glass tell the truth again.
decision: The right convex is pointed at the weather. What do you do?

options.text: Keep rolling — you still have the flat glass and the shoulder check
options.result: You guess the right-side room. A work van is in it. You find him with the skirting. The flat glass never had that angle.

options.text: Cover the dead glass with your hand so it stops lying
options.result: You drive one-handed in a work zone. The lie is gone. So is a hand. The next cone is closer than your remaining glass.

options.text: Hazards, legal pad, reset the arm until the convex sees the room again
options.result: You put the bus on a pad and put the glass back on the lane. Two minutes in the rain. The room returns. You do not buy a sideswipe with a schedule.

options.text: Switch to the left rooms only and refuse all right-side changes
options.result: The next merge is a right. You refuse it and become a rolling roadblock in a closed pattern. The work crew has to wave you through a lie you would not fix.

debrief: A mirror that does not see the lane is a maintenance problem, not a personality. Stop and set it. Guessing the right-side room is how you collect a van.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: A knocked convex must be reset before you keep changing lanes; do not drive on a blind right.

title: The Whole Front in Glass
hook: You are alongside. The pass is not done.
scene: Rain at night on Central, a box doing thirty in the right. You are in the left, mid-pass, the Ledger's nose past his cab. Recovering now would put your rear doors in his windshield. Skill nine said: see the whole front in the glass, then come back. The arterial wants you humble about how long a bus is.
decision: Your nose is past him. When do you come back?

options.text: Now — you are ahead, and the right is yours again
options.result: You recover on a guess. His windshield fills with your rear doors. He stands on it. You taught him that a pass is a suggestion.

options.text: When his whole front is in your glass and the bus is clear, then signal and recover
options.result: You wait until the box is a box in the mirror, not a wall at your hip. You signal, come back, cancel. He never had to lift. That is a finished pass.

options.text: Stay in the left after you pass — through traffic can live here
options.result: You become the new slow in the passing lane. Everyone who needed the left now needs you. Keep-right did not expire because you passed once.

options.text: Cut in tight to teach him thirty is not a speed
options.result: You give him a breath of asphalt at night in the rain. A box cannot stop on a breath. You spent his margin to make a point.

debrief: Finish the pass. Recover only when the passed vehicle's whole front is in your mirror and you are clear. Then get out of the left.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part two
source.teaching_target: Complete a multi-lane pass only when the full front of the passed vehicle is visible in the mirror.

title: The Sign Talks First
hook: The sign lights SLOW. Someone is in your doors.
scene: Snow at deep night, a volunteer box on your bumper who joined without asking. You need to dump speed for a dead pickup in the right. The stalk will talk to him late. The destination sign talks to a column. Radios are still trash. Amber is the language. If you only use the brake lamps, he eats your rear doors and you invent passengers.
decision: You need to slow and the volunteer is tight. How do you tell him?

options.text: Sign SLOW, left arm down if the lamps are buried, then lift off
options.result: Amber crawls SLOW. Your left arm goes out and down for the man who cannot see a sign through snow. He lifts. You dump speed without writing him into the doors. The pickup stays a pickup.

options.text: Stand on the brakes — the lamps are the sentence
options.result: The lamps dump. He does not. Your rear doors become his windshield. You just made passengers out of a volunteer and a schedule.

options.text: Wave him around on the left before you slow
options.result: You wave a stranger into a snow lane you have not swept. He goes. The dead pickup was not the only object. You spent him.

options.text: Leave the sign dark so you do not draw the Quiet, and hope he reads the stalk
options.result: The stalk talks for ten feet of snow. He never had a sentence. Hope is not a signal.

debrief: Tell the column before you dump speed. The destination sign is the sentence; the left arm down is the backup when snow buries the lamps. Brake lamps alone are a surprise.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: Communicate a slow-down to following traffic with the sign and, if needed, the left-arm-down signal.

title: The Straight Again
hook: Same long straight. The hood line is walking again.
scene: Overcast afternoon on 167, the same long straight. Last time your eyes left it — sleep or a screen, the mile does not care. This time the hood line is already on the rumble and the skip-dash is a smear. The thermos is still empty. A pad is coming up on the right, legal, ugly, enough. The Drift does not give second warnings. It gives the same mile twice.
decision: The hood line is on the rumble again. What do you do with the second chance?

options.text: Hold the wheel harder and finish the straight — you know it now
options.result: Knowing the mile does not put sleep in your eyes. You walk it into the rumble for real. The stack behind you writes a new shape.

options.text: Open a window and slap the dash until the line comes back
options.result: You make noise in a tired cab. The line does not come back. Mya would have, if she were here. You are not a cat.

options.text: Take the pad. Hazards. Key off. Twenty minutes you already owed.
options.result: You take the ugly pad. Key off. The log waits. When you start again the hood line is a hood line. That is the only apology the straight accepts.

options.text: Hand the wheel to whoever is in the jump — anyone awake is better
options.result: The jump is empty. You reach for a person who is not there and the rumble takes the rest.

debrief: The same straight comes back when you push through. Fatigue is still impairment the second time. Stop. The log will be there.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: A repeated lane-drift on the same stretch means stop and rest; do not tough out a second microsleep.

title: Reyna Off-Route
hook: A transit box signals out. She is not on the shelter run.
scene: Clear cold morning, downtown edge, a transit box pulling off a stop with its stalk already talking. Reyna is in a different seat today — not Bus 12, a city coach, off the shelter route, still on time. The law is the same: if she has signaled and she is coming back, you yield. The Ledger can eat a bus. The schedule cannot eat Reyna.
decision: She has signaled and the coach is coming back onto your lane. What do you do?

options.text: Hold speed — she can wait, you are already in the through lane
options.result: You keep the lane she needs. She stands on it or she clips you. She stands. You taught a transit driver that through traffic does not yield.

options.text: Pass her on the left before she commits — get it over with
options.result: You go for the left as her nose comes out. She is already in the room. Two boxes, one hole. Downtown hears it.

options.text: Horn once so she knows you see her, then keep your speed
options.result: The horn on a cold downtown edge. She flinches and stops half out. You still did not give her the lane. You just announced the block.

options.text: Lift, give her the lane, and take her back once she is through
options.result: You lift. She takes the lane she already asked for. You roll in behind her. Two fingers off the wheel, not a wave. Off-route or not, she still runs on time.

debrief: Yield to a transit vehicle in your direction that has signaled and is pulling back on. The stop is her work. The lane is the courtesy the law already named.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Yield to a transit bus in your direction that has signaled and is reentering the roadway.

title: Siren First
hook: Siren first, then lamps. Something wants the right.
scene: Rain at midday, stacked on Central. The siren arrives before the lamps — that is the order when you are in a bus. Officer Dunn is in a dark WSP remnant, lights finding the gaps, same heading, coming up the stack. The law is older than the quarantine: right, stop, wait. The Chorus would love your eyes on a screen right now. The siren is the screen.
decision: Emergency vehicle behind, siren live. What do you do?

options.text: Signal, move right, stop, wait until he is past, then reenter in order
options.result: You put the Ledger on the right and plant it. Dunn takes the hole you made. When his lamps are gone you signal and take your place in the stack. Nobody invented a new order.

options.text: Hold the left and speed up so he can have the right
options.result: You run from a siren. He needs the right, and you just filled the passing lane. The stack becomes a wall with your name on it.

options.text: Stop in your lane immediately — he can go around
options.result: You plant a bus in a live lane. He has to invent a path. The man behind you does not stop. Three vehicles, one siren, no right.

options.text: Check the tablet for which way he is going, then decide
options.result: Your eyes leave the glass. The siren is already beside you. You decide late. That was the timeout, and it was a look.

debrief: Siren or lamps: move right, stop, wait until the emergency vehicle is past, then reenter in the order you had. Do not look down to think about it.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: Pull to the right and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights or siren; reenter in original order.

title: Not a Passing Lane
hook: The diamond is empty. The box in your lane is slow.
scene: Fog at dusk on 167. A box is doing thirty in the general lane. To the left, a diamond on the pavement and a solid white fence, empty and fast. The schedule wants the hole. You are a bus. You could live in that lane. What you cannot do is dart in, pass, and dart out. That is a passing lane you invented.
decision: The diamond is empty and he is slow. Do you use it to pass?

options.text: Dart into the diamond, pass, come back before the next ramp
options.result: You use a carpool lane as a slingshot. Solid white, in and out. The remnant in the cap does not care that you are a bus. Carpool lanes are not passing lanes.

options.text: Hold the general lane. If you pass, pass in a general lane.
options.result: You stay. The diamond stays empty. When a general lane opens you take a real pass or you don't. The box keeps being thirty. You keep being legal.

options.text: Straddle the solid white until he notices and moves over
options.result: You occupy the fence. He never moves. Both lanes lose you. The diamond was not a shoulder and the solid was not a suggestion.

options.text: Take the rumble on the right and go around him there
options.result: The rumble is a drain in the fog. You put a bus in the junk to avoid a rule. He never knew you tried.

debrief: Carpool lanes are not passing lanes. A bus may travel in HOV. Darting in to pass one vehicle and coming back is not travel. Pass in a general lane, or don't.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: HOV / carpool lanes are not passing lanes; do not enter one only to pass and return.

title: Posted Is Not the Number
hook: Posted forty-five. Rain. The six seconds got longer.
scene: Rain at night on West Valley, posted forty-five, water in the wheel tracks. The Grid taught six seconds on a quiet street. At arterial speed the same seconds are more asphalt. A pickup ahead is doing the number on the sign. Your tires are doing a rumor. The Splitter loves the posted number. The road wants less.
decision: The sign says forty-five and the asphalt is a river. What speed do you keep?

options.text: Hold forty-five — posted is posted and the pickup is the proof
options.result: You match him. The next brake is a wish. The Ledger's duals write a story in the standing water. Posted was the maximum, not the assignment.

options.text: Drop to twenty and become the new problem
options.result: You become a roadblock in a live lane. The pickup goes around you in the rain. You traded a hydroplane for a sideswipe you invited.

options.text: Lift off until the six-second gap is real again, even if that is under posted
options.result: You give the water the seconds. The pickup pulls away. You can still see his tires meet the road. When the rain eases you take the number back. The sign never asked you to float.

options.text: Move left and hold forty-five in the drier tracks
options.result: The left tracks are also a river. You added a lane change on ice-that-is-rain. The number did not get safer because you switched paint.

debrief: Posted is a ceiling, not a demand. On wet asphalt, slow until your following time is real again. Arriving late is better than not arriving.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Reduce speed below posted on wet roads so following time stays usable; posted is a maximum.

title: What He Sees at the Edge
hook: The edge of his vision is not empty anymore.
scene: Ice, deep night, the Ledger in a legal pocket off Aurora. Deac's eyes are on the cage and also not. At the edge of the glass, a presence that is not a vehicle — T1, a smear that could be fatigue and could be the Quiet learning the arterial. He does not look at it. Looking is how the Chorus gets in. He names it instead, under his breath, so the student in the jump can hear: the Drift. Not a lecture. A thing that already has his lane.
debrief: The Drift is fatigue given a face. He manages it with stops and a thermos, not with stares. If you look at the edge, you have already left the road.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: Name the Drift as Deac's fatigue antagonist; do not stare at the presence at the edge of vision.

title: Both Lanes Until the Teeth
hook: Both lanes still run. The sign says the right will die.
scene: Overcast dawn, a mill-and-fill that ate the right in a quarter mile. Both lanes still move. The early-merge instinct wants the left now, to be polite, to be first. The zipper wants both lanes used until the merge paint, then one-for-one. You already took a late hole once on purpose so she could watch the cost. This is the legal late. Different sentence.
decision: The right dies ahead. When do you merge left?

options.text: Stay in the right until the merge paint, then take turns with the left
options.result: You use the lane until it ends. At the teeth you take one, give one. The stack is shorter than the polite line that started a mile early. The sign meant it.

options.text: Move left now so you are not the person who cuts at the end
options.result: You join the polite line. The right stays empty and angry. Someone late uses it and you resent them for doing the zipper. You taught the zone the wrong courtesy.

options.text: Straddle both until the last cone so nobody can beat you
options.result: You occupy two lanes in a work zone. Nobody zippers. You are the blockage the sign was trying to prevent.

options.text: Stop at the first warning sign and wait for a flagger to assign a lane
options.result: There is no flagger. You plant a bus at a sign. The zipper happens without you, around you, angry.

debrief: For a lane closure, use both lanes until the merge point, then take turns — the zipper. Early merging out of courtesy makes a longer line and a nastier end.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Zipper merge: stay in your lane until the designated merge, then alternate.

title: The Tablet Wakes
hook: The tablet wakes mid-change. The Chorus wants a look.
scene: Wind on a Kent morning, left stalk already on, hole half-taken. The aftermarket tablet on the doghouse lights up — a familiar voice, a map, a lie. II-009's cousin. Eyes off a Beetle was bad. Eyes off the Ledger mid-change is how you write a sedan into the west-coast. The timeout is the look.
decision: The screen lights up in the middle of a lane change. Where do your eyes go?

options.text: Glance the screen — one second, then finish the change
options.result: One second is a room. The sedan was in it. You find him with the arm. The Chorus got the look it wanted.

options.text: Thumb the screen off while you steer — you can do two things
options.result: You steer with a thumb on glass. The hole moves. The Ledger does not. Two things was the problem.

options.text: Finish by memory — you already swept, the screen can wait
options.result: Memory is not a sweep. The room changed. You take a hole that closed. The tablet keeps talking to nobody.

options.text: Cancel the change, hold the lane, ignore the screen, sweep again, then move
options.result: You kill the stalk and let the tablet die alone. The hole you take later is one you have seen. The Chorus does not get a vote mid-change.

debrief: A screen mid-maneuver is a look you cannot afford. Cancel, hold, finish the driving, then the glass. The Chorus can wait.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Do not take eyes off the road to a screen during a lane change; cancel and complete the driving first.

title: The Right Dual Is Soft
hook: The right dual is soft. Snow is already on the paint.
scene: Snow on an afternoon arterial. The Ledger has been wandering a half-inch toward the rumble for the last mile and it is not the Drift this time — the right dual is soft and the tread on that tire is a rumor. Two thirty-seconds is the floor. You can keep rolling on a wish or you can put the bus on a pad and know. The schedule wants the next light. The dual wants air.
decision: The right dual is soft and the tread looks thin. What do you do?

options.text: Keep rolling — a dual can run soft and the snow is only starting
options.result: You argue with rubber. The wander becomes a slide at the next brake. A dual that is soft in snow does not wait for the Drift to take the credit.

options.text: Hazards, legal pad, check tread and pressure before you take more snow
options.result: You put the bus on a pad. Tread is at the wear bars on the outer. Pressure is low. You air it from the can on the rack and you do not take the next hill on a wish. Late on the log. Rolling on purpose.

options.text: Kick it once and if it sounds hard enough, go
options.result: A kick is not a gauge. It sounds like a tire. It is still soft. The next curve writes the rest.

options.text: Overfill it by eye from the can so it cannot go soft again
options.result: You guess high. The dual is a drum. Handling gets worse, not better. The door sticker was the number. You did not read it.

debrief: Tread under two thirty-seconds slides on wet and snow. Pressure is on the door sticker, not in your foot. Stop and know. A dual that wanders is already telling you.

source.psdp_skill: n/a
source.teaching_target: Check tire tread (not less than 2/32 in) and inflation before driving on snow; do not keep rolling on a soft dual.

title: The Pass That Gains Nothing
hook: The pass would gain a length. The left is a wish.
scene: Heavy rain at dusk, two lanes, a box doing the same number you are. The left is empty for a breath. A pass would put you one length ahead and back in the same rain. Skill nine said do not pass unless you need to. Deac's thesis is shorter: if it gains nothing, it is only risk. The schedule will not notice a length. The Quiet might notice the extra noise.
decision: The left is open and he is doing your speed. Do you pass?

options.text: Pass now — empty left is permission and the schedule likes motion
options.result: You take a pass that buys a length. Recovering, you write spray across his glass. He lifts. You are one length richer and louder. The light ahead makes you even again.

options.text: Sit on his bumper until he notices and moves over
options.result: You become Hollis with a bus. He does not move. You spend the arterial as a threat. Nothing is gained except a enemy.

options.text: Flash him once so he yields the right, then take it without a pass
options.result: The flash is a demand. He brakes. You almost eat a box you did not need to pass. Permission you invented.

options.text: Hold the right. Keep the gap. Let the empty left stay empty
options.result: You stay. He stays. The left stays a lane for someone who needs it. You arrive the same minute you would have. That is the thesis: do not spend a pass you cannot cash.

debrief: Do not pass just because the left is empty. Pass to turn, to clear a hazard, to exit — not to own a length. If it gains nothing, hold.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part two
source.teaching_target: Do not change lanes or pass unnecessarily; keep right and only pass when the pass does useful work.

title: The Core From Here
hook: The Core sits ahead. Someone new is on the radio.
scene: Clear cold night, the Ledger on a legal pad at the north end of the arterial. Downtown is a dark geometry with a few stubborn lamps — the Core, locked from here. Mya has finally moved off the glass. The radio, which has been trash for two acts, carries a young voice that is not Reyna and not dispatch: a count-in, then a laugh, then static. Yuna, not yet a face. The door to Act IV is visible and shut. The log has a line left for tomorrow.
debrief: Act III ends on the arterial with the Core in sight. The next driver is already talking. The door is locked on purpose. Finish the log.
